stops.note: one proposed source: Portuguese ships passed Mauritius in the early 1500s, but no Portuguese text actually calls the bird doudo, so this derivation is disputed
the main rival source: Wybrand van Warwijck's Dutch fleet landed on Mauritius in 1598, and Dutch names for the bird included walghvogel 'nauseating bird' and dodaars 'plump-rump'
Sir Thomas Herbert described the bird in his 1634 travel book; the last widely accepted sighting was in 1662, and 'dead as a dodo' came much later, around 1900

current_meaning: an extinct flightless bird of Mauritius; something hopelessly outdated
